drg.description: Kidney and Urinary Tract Infections without MCC

notes.text:
HISTORY AND PHYSICAL. Chart, labs and overnight events reviewed. 81-year-old male admitted for urinary tract infection. Admission data:
Day 0: labs bilirubin 0.69, creatinine 0.85, hemoglobin 13.3, platelets 240, sodium 139, wbc 5.5; vitals dbp 66-70, heart_rate 72-76, map 87-91, o2_flow 0, resp_rate 13-15, sbp 126-133, spo2 96-97, temp 36.9-37
Day 0 orders/meds/results: Urinalysis: positive nitrites, >50 WBC/hpf; Ceftriaxone 1 g IV
Assessment and plan: Urinary tract infection. Hypertension.

PROGRESS NOTE, hospital day 1. Chart, labs and overnight events reviewed. Data:
Day 1: labs creatinine 0.89, hemoglobin 13.2, platelets 233, sodium 139, wbc 5.9; vitals dbp 64-69, heart_rate 71-76, map 85-90, o2_flow 0, resp_rate 13-14, sbp 127-133, spo2 96-97, temp 36.8-36.9
Day 1 orders/meds/results: Ceftriaxone 1 g IV
Assessment and plan: Urinary tract infection. Hypertension. Continue current management.

DISCHARGE SUMMARY. 81-year-old male, length of stay 2 days. Hospital course: treated per the plan above with daily labs and vital signs; stable for discharge. Medications reconciled and return precautions reviewed. Discharge diagnoses: Urinary tract infection. Hypertension. Follow up with primary care in one week. Patient seen and examined at bedside.
